gaps.note: Unrolling Q_k <= (s/W) Q_{k-1} + C gives Q_k <= (s/W)^k Q_0 + C * sum_{j<k} (s/W)^j. The page has a minus sign before the sum, which is false and does not follow from the recurrence; the added constant C contributes positively.

The sum of (s/W)^j for j<k is O((s/W)^k) only when s/W is greater than 1. The page never states that s/W>1, and only gives s/W<m^tau. If s/W<1 the sum is bounded by a constant, and if s/W=1 it equals k, so the stated bound fails or needs a separate argument. The correct statement is that the sum is O(max(1,k,(s/W)^k)), which is still O(m^{k tau}) because m^tau>1.

The page never says why m>=2; m is only the growth factor from the recursive-power-saving page. This hypothesis is needed (with tau>0) to get m^tau>1 and so absorb the constant and linear-in-k terms into O(m^{k tau}), but the reader cannot check it from what is given.
